fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), Compliance (links to VS-22), IT (links to VS-27), Store Ops (links to VS-07), DC Operations (links to VS-04), Finance (links to VS-17.4), HSE (links to VS-24), Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Annual quality/compliance planning (links to VS-31/VS-22); regulatory cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Quality define the calibration program strategy and governance" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the calibration program strategy and policy, ratify…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: Metrology authority; operational: quantified exposure and governance reporting
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fragmented-ownership risk**: Calibration split across stores/DC/facilities/IT with no single owner; mitigated by Metrology authority
- **Under-resourcing risk**: Calibration under-funded until an audit finding or revenue loss; mitigated by quantified exposure and governance reporting
System Touchpoints: - Quality (links to VS-31); compliance (links to VS-22); facilities (links to VS-07.2/VS-20.3); master data (links to VS-29); finance (links to VS-34/VS-17.4); audit (links to VS-21); IT/CMMS (links to VS-27/VS-20.3)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Quality define the calibration program strategy and governance: scope (POS/catch-weight scales, cutting equipment, paint dispensers, DC weighbridges/truck scales, fuel/logistics meters, environmental/process instruments, test & measurement tools), the regulatory map (DTI-BPS weights & measures, Consumer Act RA 7394, ISO 17025 for labs), the operating model (central standards lab + field/in-house calibration + external labs), and the KPIs (calibration currency, OOT rate, measurement variance, audit findings)

Metrology Manager establish the metrology governance: Metrology Manager role/authority, the cross-functional responsibilities (Stores/DC own the device, Metrology owns calibration, Quality owns compliance), the calibration policy, the device-classification scheme (legal-for-trade vs. process-control), and integration to quality (VS-31), facilities (VS-07.2/VS-20.3), and master data (VS-29)

Quality Manager/COO approve the calibration program strategy and policy, ratify governance/authorities, allocate the program budget (links to VS-34/VS-17.4), and report metrology posture to the quality/compliance governance (links to VS-31/VS-22) and audit (links to VS-21); communicate the mandate

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), External Calibration Labs (W3621), National Metrology Laboratory (NML-ITDI, DOST), Compliance (links to VS-22), Standards Lab (W3622)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager establish the measurement-traceability chain" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documented procedures, uncertainty budgets, environmental control, equipment,…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile the traceability chain for audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-574 (ensure controlled execution — Calibration Program, Standards & Measurement Traceability (PA-115.1).)
- operational: traceability chain and accredited labs; operational: GUM-compliant uncertainty budgets
Pain Points / Risks: - **Broken-traceability risk**: A standard calibrated to an un-traceable source invalidates all downstream calibrations; mitigated by traceability chain and accredited labs
- **Uncertainty-omission risk**: Calibration without uncertainty is incomplete; mitigated by GUM-compliant uncertainty budgets
System Touchpoints: - Standards lab (links to W3622); quality/ISO (links to VS-31); external labs (links to W3621); compliance (links to VS-22); records (links to W3624)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager establish the measurement-traceability chain: each working standard and field device traces through reference/working standards in the standards lab (W3622) to a national standard (the National Metrology Laboratory — NML under DOST-ITDI — or another recognized National Metrology Institute), with documented uncertainty per the GUM (Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement); maintain the traceability hierarchy

Metrology Manager/Quality align the in-house calibration function to ISO/IEC 17025 (general requirements for the competence of calibration/testing laboratories) where BuildRight operates an in-house standards lab (W3622): quality system, documented procedures, uncertainty budgets, environmental control, equipment, and personnel competency; pursue accreditation where it adds value

Metrology Manager maintain the reference/working standards (calibrated against national/recognized standards on cycle), manage standards custody/handling, and reconcile the traceability chain for audit (links to VS-31/VS-21/W3624); report traceability integrity to governance (W3640)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), Device Owners (Stores/DC/Services/Facilities), Compliance (links to VS-22), Standards Lab (W3622)
fields.Trigger: Program strategy (W3617); device-class definition; OOT trend (W3634)
fields.Volume: Calibration intervals and tolerances by device class

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "define calibration intervals by device class and criticality" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document the tolerance methodology" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "OOT-based interval adjustment" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-574 (ensure controlled execution — Calibration Program, Standards & Measurement Traceability (PA-115.1).)
- operational: OOT-based optimization; operational: MPE/impact-based methodology
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fixed-interval-inefficiency risk**: Over- or under-calibrating due to static intervals; mitigated by OOT-based optimization
- **Tolerance-mis-set risk**: Tolerances too tight (waste) or too loose (revenue/quality loss); mitigated by MPE/impact-based methodology
System Touchpoints: - Device registry (links to W3620/VS-29); calibration history (links to W3624/W3635); OOT (links to W3634); quality (links to VS-31); analytics (links to W3640)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager define calibration intervals by device class and criticality: legal-for-trade POS scales (statutory interval — typically annual DTI verification), cutting/paint dispensers (usage-based or time-based), DC weighbridges (statutory + usage), fuel meters (statutory), environmental instruments (time-based), test & measurement tools (usage-based); align to regulation, manufacturer, and usage

Metrology Manager define tolerances (acceptance criteria) and maximum-permissible-error (MPE) by device class and measurement: align to legal-for-trade MPE (DTI), process-control need (revenue/quality impact), and the OOT-investigation thresholds (W3634); document the tolerance methodology

Metrology Manager optimize intervals using calibration history and OOT data (W3634/W3635): extend intervals for stable devices, shorten for drift-prone ones (reliability-centered calibration / OOT-based interval adjustment); apply measurement-risk-assessment (MRA) to set economically-optimal intervals; report optimization to governance (W3640)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Master Data (links to VS-29), Device Owners (Stores/DC/Services/Facilities/IT), Procurement (links to VS-34/VS-99), Quality (links to VS-31), Finance (links to VS-35)
fields.Trigger: New device acquisition (links to VS-34/VS-99); device-class setup; registry cycle
fields.Volume: Enterprise measurement-device estate (~600 POS scales + cutting/paint/weighbridge/fuel/environmental/test devices)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Master Data register each measurement device" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "record, and report calibration" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: acquisition gate and discovery; operational: system-driven scheduling
Pain Points / Risks: - **Registry-gap risk**: Unregistered devices escape calibration; mitigated by acquisition gate and discovery
- **Master-data-staleness risk**: Wrong next-cal date causes missed calibration; mitigated by system-driven scheduling
System Touchpoints: - Item/device master (links to VS-29); fixed asset/ITAM (links to VS-35/VS-99); CMMS/calibration system (links to VS-20.3/VS-27); records (links to W3624)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Master Data register each measurement device: unique device ID/asset tag (links to VS-35/VS-99), device class, make/model/serial, location/site, measurement range, resolution, classification (legal-for-trade vs. process-control), owner, and criticality; reconcile to the fixed-asset/ITAM register (links to VS-35/VS-99)

Metrology Manager/Master Data maintain the calibration attributes per device: interval (W3619), tolerance/MPE (W3619), last/next calibration date, calibration method (in-house W3622 vs. external W3621), standards used (traceability W3618), status (due/overdue/OOT/in-service/out-of-service), and the calibration history link (W3624)

Metrology Manager/IT deploy the calibration management system / CMMS module (links to VS-27/VS-20.3) to schedule, dispatch, record, and report calibration; integrate to the device registry and trigger alerts for due/overdue (links to W3622/W3632); audit registry completeness

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Procurement (links to VS-34), Quality (links to VS-31), Compliance (links to VS-22), Vendor Mgmt (links to VS-03), Finance (links to VS-17)
fields.Trigger: Calibration outsourcing decision; lab sourcing; lab performance review

workflows.name: External Calibration Lab Qualification & Vendor Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Procurement define external-lab qualification criteria" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "Metrology Manager/Procurement qualify and contract external labs" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-route of "route devices to the optimal lab" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-574 (ensure controlled execution — Calibration Program, Standards & Measurement Traceability (PA-115.1).)
- operational: accreditation-scope verification; operational: SLA and dual-sourcing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-accredited-lab risk**: Lab without proper ISO 17025 scope invalidates calibration; mitigated by accreditation-scope verification
- **Turnaround risk**: Lab backlog takes devices out of service; mitigated by SLA and dual-sourcing
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-34/VS-03); quality/ISO (links to VS-31); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67); device registry (links to W3620); records (links to W3624)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Procurement define external-lab qualification criteria: ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation scope (the lab must be accredited for the specific calibration), traceability to national/international standards (W3618), uncertainty capability, turnaround, geographic coverage (on-site for weighbridges/large devices), and accreditation-body recognition (PAB or ILAC-MRA signatory)

Metrology Manager/Procurement qualify and contract external labs: due diligence (accreditation certificate/scope verification), contract (scope, turnaround, uncertainty, recall/OOT notification, liability), rate/SLA, and the approved-lab list; integrate to vendor management (links to VS-03) and the scorecard (links to VS-67)

Metrology Manager manage external-lab performance: monitor turnaround, quality (calibration acceptance, OOT notification), accreditation currency, and cost; re-qualify periodically, manage the approved lab list, and route devices to the optimal lab (in-house vs. external); report to governance (W3640)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Calibration Technicians (W3623), Standards Lab, Device Owners (Stores/DC/Services/Facilities), Quality (links to VS-31), IT/CMMS (links to VS-27/VS-20.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Standards Lab operate the in-house calibration function" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "Calibration Technicians perform calibration per documented procedure and tolerance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report in-house throughput/quality to governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-574 (ensure controlled execution — Calibration Program, Standards & Measurement Traceability (PA-115.1).)
- operational: reference-standard re-calibration cycle; operational: procedures, competency (W3623), and MSA (W3638)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Standard-degradation risk**: In-house reference standard drifts, propagating error; mitigated by reference-standard re-calibration cycle
- **Skill-error risk**: Technician error invalidates calibration; mitigated by procedures, competency (W3623), and MSA (W3638)
System Touchpoints: - CMMS/calibration system (links to VS-20.3/VS-27/W3620); standards/traceability (links to W3618); records (links to W3624); OOT (links to W3634); quality (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Standards Lab operate the in-house calibration function: schedule and dispatch calibration (CMMS-driven links to W3620), calibrate field/portable devices (POS scale verification, cutting/paint dispensers, environmental instruments, test tools) using reference/working standards (W3618), perform on-site calibration for installed devices (weighbridges, large scales, fuel meters)
steps.r: Metrology Manager / Calibration Technicians / Standards Lab

steps.activity: Calibration Technicians perform calibration per documented procedure and tolerance (W3619): pre-check, as-found verification, adjustment, as-left verification, uncertainty estimation, pass/fail/OOT determination (links to W3634), labeling/sealing (legal-for-trade seals), and the calibration certificate/record (W3624); return to service or quarantine if OOT

Metrology Manager/Standards Lab maintain the standards lab environment (temperature/humidity/control per ISO 17025 where applicable), reference/working-standard custody and re-calibration (W3618), and consumables/tools; manage the in-house vs. external routing decision (W3621); report in-house throughput/quality to governance (W3640)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, HR/L&D (links to VS-19.3/VS-103), Quality (links to VS-31), Standards Lab, Device Operators (Stores/DC/Services)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/HR define calibration competency requirements" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "Metrology Manager/L&D deliver training" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track certification/expiry and refresher, audit competency coverage, and feed…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: certification gating; operational: refresher and competency audit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uncertified-technician risk**: Untrained staff calibrating produces invalid results; mitigated by certification gating
- **Skill-atrophy risk**: Infrequent calibration erodes skill; mitigated by refresher and competency audit
System Touchpoints: - HR/L&D (links to VS-19.3/VS-103); quality (links to VS-31); records (links to VS-88); competency register

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/HR define calibration competency requirements: calibration technicians (metrology fundamentals, uncertainty, procedures by device class, MSA/Gage R&R), and device operators (correct use, basic checks, defect reporting); define the certification/qualification scheme

Metrology Manager/L&D deliver training: classroom and hands-on, device-class procedures, software/CMMS, standards handling, and safety (electrical/pressure for some instruments); certify technicians and record competency; manage external certifications where required

Metrology Manager maintain the competency register, track certification/expiry and refresher, audit competency coverage, and feed gaps to L&D (links to VS-19.3); report to governance (W3640) and audit (links to VS-21)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), Calibration Technicians, Compliance (links to VS-22), Records (links to VS-88), Audit (links to VS-21), External Labs (W3621)
fields.Trigger: Per calibration; annual audit; regulatory inspection

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager produce the calibration record/certificate per calibration" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "Metrology Manager/Quality maintain calibration documentation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "Metrology Manager/Audit conduct the annual calibration audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: documentation discipline; operational: closure tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Records-gap risk**: Missing calibration records fail audit/inspection and invalidate legal-for-trade status; mitigated by documentation discipline
- **Audit-finding-accumulation risk**: Findings not remediated; mitigated by closure tracking
System Touchpoints: - Calibration system/records (links to VS-20.3/VS-27); records retention (links to VS-88); quality/ISO (links to VS-31); audit (links to VS-21); compliance (links to VS-22/W3633)

steps.activity: Calibration Technicians/Metrology Manager produce the calibration record/certificate per calibration: device, date, technician/lab, standards used (traceability W3618), as-found/as-left results, tolerance/MPE (W3619), uncertainty, pass/fail/OOT (W3634), adjustments, and the next-due date; sign/issue and store in the calibration system

Metrology Manager/Quality maintain calibration documentation: certificates, procedures, uncertainty budgets, traceability chain (W3618), training records (W3623), lab accreditations (W3621), and the calibration register; retention per regulation/VS-88 (legal-for-trade typically 3–7 years); manage legal-for-trade seals/labels

Metrology Manager/Audit conduct the annual calibration audit: registry completeness (W3620), schedule adherence, OOT handling (W3634), records quality, traceability integrity (W3618), and ISO 17025 conformance where applicable; support DTI/regulatory inspection (links to VS-22/W3633) and manage findings to closure; report to governance (W3640)
